comments.why: Excellent short piece on Terraform's synthetic fuel approach.
comments.text: Related, and yet not mentioned in TFA: "Terraform makes carbon neutral natural gas" [LINK] Excellent S3 piece on Terraform [20min]: [VIDEO] I agree with Terraform's founder on at least one thing: atmospheric carbon capture needs to be cheaper than ground extraction. Market forces will decide the rest. This is not a CO2 cop-out, we need to both stop introducing CO2 into the atmosphere, and also extract gigatons from it. Terraform Industries is addressing both sides.

comments.story: Energy economics and rocket science with Casey Handmer
comments.why: Tour of Terraform and its goals from the founder.
comments.text: Casey Handmer's company is creating synthetic hydrocarbons from renewable energy. Here is a good video where he gives a tour of the company and talks about its goals: [VIDEO] . Curious what people think about the idea of synthetic hydrocarbons? It is a seemingly obvious idea that I hadn't heard about until recently, as long as you can use energy efficiently to create the synthetic hydrocarbons.

comments.author: bryanlarsen
comments.story: Terraform makes carbon neutral natural gas
comments.why: States Terraform's cost goals for carbon capture and hydrogen.
comments.text: On [VIDEO] he says the goal is $100/tonne carbon capture and $1/kg H2, which puts those inputs well under the $10/kcf leaving some margin for the cost of the sabatier. Both processes are directly proportional to the cost of electricity and heat so assuming the thesis of decreasing solar costs holds true, it's a question of when not if.
